title: Industry sponsorship and research outcome
finding: Efficacy favorable RR 1.27 (95% CI 1.17–1.37); conclusions favorable RR 1.34 (1.19–1.51); harms RR 1.37 (.64–2.93). Drug/device studies, not a universal correction.
status: staged methodological evidence or research lead; no automatic publication

title: Association of Industry Sponsorship With Outcomes of Nutrition Studies
finding: Favorable conclusions RR 1.31 (.99–1.72); uncertainty includes null; nutrition evidence not equivalent to drug/device evidence.
status: staged methodological evidence or research lead; no automatic publication

title: Conduct and reporting of formula milk trials
finding: 100/125 high RoB; 5/125 low RoB; 98/117 with reported funding industry-supported; 60/81 with clear role industry involved analysis/report; 17/125 low COI by review criteria. Effect size not related to commercial involvement in superiority subset, high RoB associated with favorable conclusions.
funding: Imperial Health Charity support; lead author declared outside-work ties including expert witness formula claims and personal fees; full disclosures to extract
status: staged methodological evidence or research lead; no automatic publication

title: Assessing conflict of interest reporting and quality of clinical trials on infant formula
finding: Fortified formula trials often high risk of bias; overlap with P1-03 unresolved.
status: staged methodological evidence or research lead; no automatic publication

title: Health and nutrition claims for infant formula: international cross sectional survey
finding: Many claims lack robust clinical support; distinguish marketing claim evidence from nutritional adequacy. Not a clinical outcome study.
status: staged methodological evidence or research lead; no automatic publication

title: Effects of Early Toilet Training and Elimination Communication With Respect to Diaper Types
finding: Cloth and more diaper-free time associated with earlier toilet training. Confounding and definitions require extraction.
status: staged methodological evidence or research lead; no automatic publication

title: Do disposable diapers reduce urination elimination signals in non-toilet-trained children?
finding: 23 of 28 complete; reduced urination signals wearing diapers; not actual age of training completion.
funding: pending; check possible overlap with P1-08
status: staged methodological evidence or research lead; no automatic publication

title: Measuring the impact of disposable diapers on urination elimination signals in non-toilet-trained children
finding: Observe with and without diaper. Check sample identity with P1-07; no independent count yet.
funding: authors report no specific grant, no competing interests (indexed PMID 40640001)
status: staged methodological evidence or research lead; no automatic publication

title: Assisted Infant Toilet Training and Bladder and Bowel Health: A Global Integrative Review
finding: Observational findings potentially protective but serious risk of bias. Review reports cultural variation and evidence gaps.
funding: open access support CAUL/member institutions; no declared COI
status: staged methodological evidence or research lead; no automatic publication

title: Assisted infant toilet training and the prevalence of functional gastrointestinal disorders up to the age of 9 months: a randomised, controlled trial
design: BABITT ongoing Swedish RCT, early endpoint
finding: Early assisted training at moderate frequency did not reduce functional GI disorders by nine months. Long-term continence outcomes not established.
access: indexed publisher results and funding; full page blocked
funding: Region Dalarna, Regional Research Council Uppsala–Örebro, Mayflower Association, Samaritan Foundation for Paediatric Research, Swedish Enuresis Academy; full COI pending
status: staged methodological evidence or research lead; no automatic publication

title: Does the development and use of modern disposable diapers affect bladder control? A systematic review
finding: Relevant historical and clinical synthesis; full funding statement and study membership needed before interpretation.
funding: commercial involvement flagged in indexed disclosure; exact sponsor and role pending
status: staged methodological evidence or research lead; no automatic publication

title: A child-oriented approach to toilet training
finding: 1170 records; mean daytime training 28.5 months; cannot infer historical causal diaper effect.
funding: historical funding and later industry ties must be documented separately
status: staged methodological evidence or research lead; no automatic publication

title: Choosing an Infant Formula
finding: Regulated commercial infant formula meets minimum nutrient and safety requirements; homemade formula unsafe.
funding: government guidance; panel/underlying evidence review separate
